hazards.title: Automatic startup movement
controls: Treat every first actuator energization after an applicable change as a possible-motion event.
Clear and observe the complete startup swept volume with devices and contact tools removed.
Require an independent physical power-cut E-stop and forbid host initialization, homing, parking, or automatic retry.
required_evidence: Reviewed empty-cell startup-swept-volume inspection and observer positions.
Continuous record binding manual power application, zero host commands, actual startup behavior, and final disconnected state.
Observed power-cut consequence and incident disposition for any unexpected or uncertain movement.

hazards.title: Gravity drop or stored-energy movement
controls: Install passive gravity-safe containment, a catch, support, counterbalance, or a proven safe-collapse envelope.
Test power loss using a dummy load at representative poses before devices or contact tools are installed.
Keep personnel and fragile articles outside both powered and unpowered swept volumes.
required_evidence: Reviewed containment identity, attachment, clearance, and retained-condition photographs.
Repeated representative-pose power-loss observations including residual travel, settling, and stored-energy release.
Evidence that E-stop power removal does not create a more hazardous uncontrolled collapse.

hazards.title: Pinch crush or collision injury
controls: Maintain a cleared keepout around every arm link, tool, fixture, cable, and startup or route swept volume.
Require reviewed collision geometry, conservative limits, reduced-speed empty-cell trials, and an observer at the cutoff.
Keep descent and contact independently blocked throughout onboarding and noncontact acceptance.
required_evidence: Installed-object inventory and collision model bound to the retained arm, tool, support, fixtures, and cable routes.
Observed reduced-speed stop, clearance, settling, and safe-park trials over the approved empty-cell routes.
Incident-free noncontact acceptance record with explicit minimum clearances and rejected-route evidence.

hazards.title: E-stop or cutoff path ineffective
controls: Use a physical actuator-power cutoff independent of host software and reachable by the observer.
Qualify the cutoff first on an inert load, including latch, reset, discharge, and USB back-power behavior.
Require a fresh reviewed energization permit and reject automatic restart after reset or mains return.
required_evidence: Power topology and wiring inspection identifying every supply, return, cutoff, and possible back-power path.
Repeated voltage-removal and reset tests with measured downstream state and accessible observer actuation.
First-power record showing the cutoff remained effective in the installed configuration.

hazards.title: Polarity overcurrent heat or fire
controls: Verify exact supply identity, voltage, polarity, current capacity, connector pinout, conductor rating, and protective devices while disconnected.
Perform initial electrical checks on an inert load with current limiting and a suitable means of isolation.
Reject damaged, warm, loose, improvised, or ambiguous power components and connectors.
required_evidence: Received supply, cable, connector, fuse, and cutoff identities with polarity and continuity measurements.
Inert-load voltage, current, temperature, and isolation observations retained with the reviewed procedure.
Inspection confirming strain relief, conductor protection, connector retention, and absence of unsafe heating.

hazards.title: Serial open resets controller or causes movement
controls: Bind one persistent controller identity before opening and configure RTS and DTR false.
Durably consume a fresh manual permit before the single bounded serial-open attempt.
Send only one allowlisted feedback request after a quiet-buffer check; close on reset, drift, timeout, or malformed response without retry.
required_evidence: Power-off controller identity and serial profile bound to the exact received arm and firmware.
Raw, timed record of open behavior, receive-buffer state, one T=105 request, one T=1051 response, and close.
Observed controller reset and movement classification with effect certainty and final power state.

hazards.title: Camera support or gantry falls or shifts
controls: Retain a reviewed support, fastener, keeper, tether, ballast, and bench attachment configuration.
Use witness marks and drift checks; any bump, reseat, loosened fastener, or moved bench invalidates dependent evidence.
Keep support members and the camera outside the qualified arm envelope with conservative clearance.
required_evidence: Installed support identity, dimensions, fastener engagement, keeper or tether, and anti-tip evidence.
Static load, bump, reseat, and repeated camera-to-board drift measurements.
Installed collision and clearance review covering camera, gantry, clamps, fasteners, and all arm poses.

hazards.title: USB or tool cable snag and pull
controls: Route static and moving cables with controlled service loops, strain relief, connector retention, and separation from swept volumes.
Model the retained cable route as installed collision geometry and prohibit temporary or hanging leads.
Stop on cable contact, tension, disconnect, route drift, or unreviewed harness change.
required_evidence: Retained cable and connector identities, routing photographs, bend radii, service-loop dimensions, and strain-relief inspection.
Full-range empty-cell sweep observations for snag, pull, flex, connector motion, and occlusion.
Post-sweep identity, continuity, support-drift, and cable-route witness checks.

hazards.title: Wrong or substituted device identity
controls: Bind model, VID, PID, unit serial, persistent OS identity, host port, driver, and received-article evidence before device access.
Reject ambiguous candidates, numeric camera indexes, bare COM names, backend fallback, and operator-selected substitutes.
Recheck persistent identity after acquiring the device lease and after every close, reconnect, reboot, or driver change.
required_evidence: Received labels and power-off inventory correlated with one persistent camera and one persistent controller identity.
Reconnect and reboot stability observations with candidate enumeration and explicit ambiguity results.
Open-time identity and selected mode receipt matching the precommitted device binding.

hazards.title: Stale calibration localization or UI map
controls: Bind every calibration, target map, UI state, and derived artifact to exact parent hashes and configuration epochs.
Invalidate descendants after any camera, support, tag, arm, tool, keyboard, phone, operating-system, IME, orientation, scale, or theme change.
Require fresh localization and quality gates before every descent and prohibit nominal or simulation fallback.
required_evidence: Complete dependency graph and epoch records linking installed hardware, settings, calibrations, maps, and observers.
Training and independent held-out residuals plus repeated installation, bump, reseat, and drift validation.
Fresh pre-action observation binding the current board, device, UI state, pose, settings, and accepted calibration hashes.

hazards.title: Automatic retry duplicates a physical effect
controls: Write and durably seal an attempt intent before every operation that can affect a device or the physical cell.
Never replay an in-flight attempt after timeout, crash, disconnect, or uncertain completion.
Require manual reconciliation and a newly reviewed attempt; latch global quarantine when an external effect is uncertain.
required_evidence: Append-only attempt ledger covering intent, device-I/O start and finish, sealed evidence, assessment, and effect certainty.
Crash, timeout, reconnect, torn-tail, and duplicate-request tests proving resume performs verification only.
Manual reconciliation record identifying the prior attempt and authorizing or denying a distinct next attempt.

hazards.title: Concurrent sessions or processes touch one device
controls: Acquire leases only in canonical order CELL -> SESSION -> CAMERA -> ARM_CONTROLLER, with one mutable physical session per cell.
Recheck device identity after lock acquisition and deny every second caller before device open.
Do not break a stale lease using PID alone; require conservative owner and durability reconciliation.
required_evidence: Cross-process contention tests showing exactly one owner and zero device calls by denied contenders.
Crash, stale-owner, PID-reuse, and Windows lock-durability tests with no automatic takeover or replay.
Lease and device-identity records bound into every effectful attempt.

hazards.title: Calibration motion requires unavailable calibration
controls: Use a separately reviewed, external, contained precalibration bootstrap rather than nominal task calibration.
Limit bootstrap motion to a conservative surveyed empty-cell envelope with devices removed, reduced limits, independent observation, and fresh permits.
Never treat automatic middle-position startup motion, a commanded pose, or vendor nominal geometry as calibrated home.
required_evidence: Bootstrap plan and command allowlist bound to the retained arm, tool-free state, surveyed envelope, collision geometry, and power controls.
Actual stop, gravity, power-loss, achieved-feedback, and controller-model-correlation evidence from diverse bounded poses.
Independent review separating bootstrap evidence from the final reference-frame calibration and its held-out acceptance.

hazards.title: Tool damages keyboard or phone
controls: Keep all descent and contact blocked until tool retention, TCP, compliance, travel, force, target safe regions, and outcome observation are independently qualified.
Qualify keyboard and phone contact separately, starting with nondestructive dummy articles and purpose-built large targets.
Retract and inspect after one attempt; never retry an ambiguous contact or infer success from a command.
required_evidence: Retained tool and device identities with measured surface, target, footprint, compliance, force, travel, and uncertainty budgets.
Dummy-contact and device-specific single-contact trials with achieved pose, independent outcome, inspection, and no-damage evidence.
Separate reviewed keyboard and phone release decisions with explicit scope and current dependency hashes.

hazards.title: Camera evidence exposes private screen content
controls: Use controlled nonprivate test content and remove unrelated screens, documents, people, and identifiers from the camera view.
Retain raw evidence locally with least-privilege access, explicit retention rules, and no automatic upload.
Generate previews through bounded safe re-encoding and reviewed cropping or redaction rather than exposing raw frames.
required_evidence: Reviewed scene-clearance, data-classification, access, export, deletion, and incident-response procedure.
Manifest identifying every raw and derived image, its purpose, custodian, retention state, and authorized exports.
Tests showing previews do not embed raw metadata or pixels outside the approved field of view.

hazards.title: Operator observer or reviewer role confusion
controls: Name operator, observer, and reviewer explicitly for each controlled attempt and show their duties before permitting work.
Require operator and observer to differ for energization, and operator and reviewer to differ for power-safety and effect reviews.
Treat role records as fresh attestations rather than identity authentication and deny expired, missing, ambiguous, or conflicting attestations.
required_evidence: Attempt-bound role attestations, procedure acknowledgements, timestamps, and required inequality checks.
Observer confirmation of cutoff access, cleared cell, communication protocol, and authority to stop the attempt.
Independent review record for power safety, uncertain effects, incidents, and any scoped physical release.
